subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Dodge Brothers
description: A fast breakdown of The Dodge Brothers for builders.

hook.text: John and Horace Dodge built parts for Ford before deciding they could build a better car themselves.

buildup.text: They supplied Ford with engines and axles—without the Dodges, the Model T couldn't have existed.

discovery.text: In 1914, they launched their own car. It was tougher and more powerful than the Model T.

twist.text: Both brothers died within a year of each other in 1920, cutting short a promising rivalry.

climax.text: Their company changed hands many times and eventually became part of Chrysler, then Stellantis.

punchline.text: Ford's best suppliers became his fiercest competitors.

quiz.question: What did the Dodge brothers supply to Ford?

details.summary: John and Horace Dodge built precision parts for Ford before launching their own car company in 1914, creating tough, reliable vehicles that outsold nearly every competitor within five years.
details.whyItMatters: The Dodge brothers demonstrated that supplier expertise could translate into competitive car manufacturing. Their mechanical precision and durability set standards the brand carries to this day.
takeaways: They supplied engines and chassis parts to Henry Ford
Their first car launched in 1914 with an all-steel body
Both brothers died within a year of each other in 1920

faq.question: Why did the Dodge brothers leave Ford?
faq.answer: They wanted to build their own cars rather than remain suppliers. They also grew frustrated as Ford increasingly tried to reduce supplier dependence and bring manufacturing in-house.

faq.question: What happened to Dodge after the brothers died?
faq.answer: The company was sold to Chrysler in 1928. Dodge became Chrysler's volume brand, eventually gaining a performance reputation with muscle cars like the Charger and Challenger in the 1960s and beyond.
